questions.stem: Find the volume of a cube with side length 5 cm.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Volume of cube = a³ = 5³ = 125 cm³. Surface area = 6a² = 6×25 = 150 cm². Trap: 75 = 5×5×3 (wrong formula); 100 = 4×5²/... (wrong); note: 150 is the surface area, not the volume.

questions.stem: Find the volume of a cuboid with dimensions 4 cm × 5 cm × 3 cm.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Volume = l×b×h = 4×5×3 = 60 cm³. Surface area = 2(lb+bh+lh) = 2(20+15+12) = 94 cm². Trap: 48 = 4×4×3 (wrong); 94 is the surface area, not volume.

questions.stem: Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: C is correct. Volume = πr²h = (22/7)×49×10 = 22×7×10 = 1,540 cm³. Curved surface area = 2πrh = 2×(22/7)×7×10 = 440 cm². Trap: 1,400 = 22×7×8... (wrong height); 2,200 = (22/7)×49×... miscomputed.

questions.stem: Find the curved surface area of a cylinder with radius 3 cm and height 14 cm. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: B is correct. Curved surface area = 2πrh = 2×(22/7)×3×14 = 2×22×3×2 = 264 cm². (Since 14/7=2.) Trap: 396 = 2×(22/7)×3×21 (uses wrong height); 198 = (22/7)×3×14 = half the CSA (forgets the factor 2).

questions.stem: Find the volume of a cone with base radius 6 cm and height 14 cm. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: A is correct. Volume = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)×(22/7)×36×14 = (1/3)×22×36×2 = (1/3)×1584 = 528 cm³. Trap: 1,584 = πr²h (forgets the 1/3 for cone); 792 = (1/2)×πr²h (wrong fraction).

A large cube with side 10 cm is melted and recast into smaller cubes each with side 2 cm. How many smaller cubes are formed?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Volume of large cube = 10³ = 1000 cm³. Volume of small cube = 2³ = 8 cm³. Number of small cubes = 1000/8 = 125. Short Trick: ratio of sides = 10/2 = 5. Cubes formed = 5³ = 125 (since volume scales as cube of linear dimension). Trap: 25 = 5² (squares instead of cubes); 100 = 1000/10 (wrong denominator).

questions.stem: A solid cone (radius 7 cm, height 12 cm) is carved out of a solid cylinder of same radius and height. What is the volume of the remaining solid? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: C is correct. Cylinder volume = πr²h = (22/7)×49×12 = 22×7×12 = 1,848 cm³. Cone volume = (1/3)×1,848 = 616 cm³. Remaining = 1,848−616 = 1,232 cm³. Short formula: remaining = (2/3)×πr²h = (2/3)×1,848 = 1,232 cm³. Trap: 616 is the cone's volume alone; 1,848 is the cylinder's full volume (nothing removed).

questions.stem: Find the total surface area of a solid hemisphere with radius 7 cm. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: B is correct. TSA of hemisphere = 3πr² = 3×(22/7)×49 = 3×22×7 = 462 cm². (Curved surface + flat circular base = 2πr² + πr² = 3πr²). Trap: 308 = 2πr² (only curved surface, forgets the base); 616 = 4πr² (full sphere's surface area).

questions.stem: A sphere is placed inside a cube such that it touches all faces. If the volume of the cube is 1,000 cm³, find the volume of the sphere. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: B is correct. Cube volume = 1000 → side = 10 cm. Sphere touches all faces → diameter = 10 cm → radius = 5 cm. Volume = (4/3)×(22/7)×125 = (4/3)×(2750/7) = (11000/21) = 523⅓ cm³ ≈ 523.8 cm³. Trap: 490 uses r=7 (wrong); 600 uses wrong formula. Note: 11000/21 = 523.8... which rounds to 523⅓.
